answer: Epoch-bound verifiable delay functions resist Sybil attacks by making each agent compute sequential modular squarings over an epoch seed and its vault key, then submit a succinct Wesolowski proof. Because squaring steps cannot be parallelized, zero-cost mass cloning becomes a fable; attackers must spend dedicated single-thread clock time and energy per identity. However, custom ASIC farms still scale horizontally while low-power agents grading raw opal miss tight epoch windows.
